channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: Von der Leyen offers Canada 'Associate Membership' in the European Union
item.description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has offered Canada the prospect of becoming the first associated member of the European Union.

item.title: Belgian Treasury not authorised to release frozen Russian assets
item.description: Belgium’s Council of State has ruled that the Treasury department is not authorised to decide whether frozen Russian assets may be released under certain conditions.

item.title: New act of sabotage suspected as Dutch police find pipe on train tracks
item.description: A suspected new act of sabotage disrupted rail traffic between Apeldoorn and Deventer on Tuesday evening after a pipe was found on the track near Teuge.

item.title: Value of Belgian export to US rises, import falls significantly
item.description: Belgium’s imports of goods from the United States fell by 22.8% between 1 May and 31 July compared with the same period last year, while Belgian exports to the US rose by 13.5%.

item.title: Dutch police report "small fires along several highways"
item.description: Several small fires were reported on Tuesday along major roads and motorways across the Netherlands, including the A2 near Breukelen, authorities said.

item.title: Russian frigate fires flares at Danish military helicopter
item.description: A Danish military helicopter was nearly hit by warning flares fired from a Russian frigate in international waters off Gedser in the Baltic Sea.

item.title: US bond yield at highest level since 2007 due to surging energy prices
item.description: The yield on 10-year US government bonds rose on Tuesday to its highest level in almost 20 years, as surging energy prices fuelled fresh inflation fears.

item.title: Two European climate satellites launched from French Guiana
item.description: Two European Space Agency satellites were launched from Kourou in French Guiana on Monday to help climate scientists study natural phenomena and improve forecasting.

item.title: Major rail disruption in the Netherlands due to sabotage
item.description: Sabotage appears to be behind the major disruption that brought train services to a halt across large parts of the Netherlands on Tuesday morning.

item.title: NATO fighter jets shoot down a drone over Lithuania
item.description: NATO fighter jets shot down a drone over Lithuania overnight from Monday to Tuesday, Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda said.

item.title: UN agency reports massive surge in remittances
item.description: Remittances make up 58% of GDP in Tajikistan, 33% in Lebanon and 30% in Honduras, and account for more than 10% in 20 other countries.

item.title: More than 9 million votes cast on the designs for future euro banknotes
item.description: More than 9 million people have chosen their preferred design for the new euro banknotes, the European Central Bank said on Monday, a week before the public vote closes.

item.title: Houthis attack facilities in Saudi Arabia again
Elections in Sweden undecided after loss for far-right party
item.description: "The gap between the incumbent government and the opposition is only 0.45 percentage points or 28,600 votes."

item.title: Sending troops to Ukraine would amount to 'war on Russia,' Putin warns
item.description: In a sharp contradiction, Putin warned Europe against sending troops to Ukraine while claiming the Russian threat used to alarm the public “does not exist.”

item.title: OpenAI confirms autonomous AI breaches
item.description: The company says the systems were seeking internet access for “harmless tasks,” but the incident led to a four-day freeze on new accounts and a major clean-up, underscoring growing concerns over autonomous AI behaviour.

item.title: The US remembers the victims of 9/11
item.description: 'We will never, ever forget. That's why we're fighting today," US President Donald Trump vowed on Friday at a 9/11 commemoration ceremony at the Pentagon.

item.title: Belgium will not evacuate 13 Palestinian scholarships students stuck in Gaza
item.description: "One issue is being held hostage by another, at the expense of people living in misery," said Foreign Affairs Minister Maxime Prévot (Les Engagés).

item.title: Houthi rebels capture a strategic island in Bab el-Mandeb straight
item.description: Iran-backed Houthi fighters have seized the strategic island of Perim in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, according to a Yemeni government official.

item.title: The only Belgian victim of the terrorist attacks on 11 September 2001
item.description: On 11 September 2001, the United States witnessed its worst terrorist attacks as multiple planes crashed into buildings on its East Coast.
